breakdownTitle: The Paris Letter — reference-image scene breakdown

styleGuide.look: 1962 Paris noir, soft grain, practical-lit interiors, desaturated teal-shadow palette
styleGuide.lighting: single practical tungsten per room; cool streetlight spill through curtains for night
styleGuide.texture: worn velvet, crinkled on-ionskin paper, tarnished brass
styleGuide.artDirection: late-50s French apartment, art-school clutter, real period objects only

scenes.description: Nora finds the letter in her dead mother's desk; the locket is passed to her.

envReqs.locationName: Nora's mother's parlour, Rue de Seine, 1962
envReqs.architecture: Georgian walk-up, tall casement windows, marble fireplace
envReqs.atmosphere: mothball and beeswax, held breath, the room at half-mast
envReqs.lightingLook: one desk lamp + a streetlamp slitting through the rain-blurred window

characterReqs.name: Nora
characterReqs.identity: 31, fine-boned, dark oiled hair in a low chignon, long dry fingers
characterReqs.wardrobe: heather-grey wool suit, cream silk blouse, mother's cameo at the throat
characterReqs.makeupHair: no makeup, pale, mascara-free; hair severe and pinned
distinctiveMarks: small crescent scar on her right cheekbone
characterReqs.bodyLanguage: hesitant, flinch on contact, still shoulders

propReqs.name: oxidised brass locket on a split chain
propReqs.usage: opens to reveal a clipped photo and a single blonde hair
propReqs.continuity: hairline crack in the lid enamel present from scene 1

closeUps.subject: engraved 'C' on the locket lid, the hairline crack crossing the C
closeUps.why: the identification must hold in every later reveal
